body:
Advent International has raised $30 billion across its global funds, including nearly $27 billion for its 11th flagship global private equity fund, GPE XI, the firm said in a press release.

GPE XI exceeded its fundraising target of $26 billion. Advent described it as the largest buyout fund to complete fundraising so far in 2026. Its new mid-market strategy, launched in March, has secured more than $3 billion in commitments.

Advent said 2026 has been one of its strongest years for realisations, with about $13 billion realised across 27 businesses. The firm has also invested around $10 billion across 38 new and existing businesses so far this year, including completed and pending deals.

Advent's India investments

Advent has invested more than $5.6 billion in India across 23 investments since entering the market in October 2007 with an investment in CAMS. The firm opened its Mumbai office in 2009.

Its Indian investments include Yatharth Hospitals, Iscon Balaji, Aditya Birla Housing Finance, Svatantra and Apollo 24/7, according to the press release. Felix Pharma is among its more recent investments.

Advent's recent exits in India include Birla Capital in October 2025, Manjushree in March 2025 and BSV in October 2024.

“We’re proud to have raised $30 billion across our global fund complex and excited about what it means for India,” said Shweta Jalan, managing partner at Advent International.

Jalan said the fundraising reinforced the firm's commitment to India and its focus on partnering with businesses to support their growth.

New strategy targets mid-market companies

Advent's new mid-market strategy will target smaller buyouts and growth investments, with equity investments ranging from $100 million to $350 million in companies with enterprise values of up to $1.25 billion. The strategy will focus primarily on North America and Europe.

GPE XI will invest across geographies, sectors, deal types and sizes, with a focus on Europe and North America. Advent also operates in Asia-Pacific and has a regional team in Latin America.

The firm said commitments to its funds came from new and existing investors, including public and private pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments and foundations, institutional fund managers, family offices and high-net-worth individuals.

Advent has more than 290 investment professionals working across business and financial services, consumer, healthcare, industrial and technology sectors. Since 2024, it has opened offices in Sydney, Tokyo and Abu Dhabi. In early 2026, it strengthened its presence in Hong Kong to support investor engagement across Asia-Pacific.
